input: A capital appraisal has been carried out in respect of a proposed bottling line, and the results of the appraisal are summarised as follows. The installed cost of the line is $788k, and the expected net saving arising from its operation is $171k per year, over an expected life of 8 years. When the savings are discounted at a discount rate of 6%, the present value of the savings amounts to $1062k, and, after the installed cost has been taken into account, the net present value of the project is $274k. On the face of it, therefore, the appraisal indicates that the line would more than repay its installed cost over the period in question, with the discounted savings exceeding the cost by a comfortable margin. It should nevertheless be borne in mind that the savings on which the appraisal rests are vendor and utility estimates, and that no saving of this kind has yet been measured on a comparable installation in practice. The figures should accordingly be regarded as estimates that have been prepared on a consistent basis for the purposes of the appraisal, rather than as amounts that have been demonstrated, and the positive net present value should be read in that light when the proposal comes to be considered.
target: The bottling line has a net present value of $274k at a discount rate of 6%, on savings that are estimates and have not been measured on a comparable installation. The installed cost is $788k. The expected net saving is $171k per year for 8 years, and the present value of the savings at the stated rate is $1062k. The net present value is the excess of that present value over the installed cost: discounting reduces the savings to their value at the appraisal date, and the comparison is made in money of the same date. A positive result states that the discounted savings cover the installed cost with a margin. The discount rate is the price the appraisal puts on waiting for the savings, and a higher rate would reduce the present value of the same savings stream. The margin is not a measured return. The savings are vendor and utility estimates, and no saving has yet been measured on a comparable installation, so the appraisal's result stands or falls with estimates that operating experience has not tested. The appraisal also prices time only through the discount rate: it states what the savings stream is worth against the cost today, and it says nothing about the risk that the savings arrive late or unevenly across the life of the line.
